evals.prompt: Make the tracking look only for traffic cones and people, at one frame a second.
evals.expected_output: One code write on the Track Objects node walk-objects that sets LABELS to ["traffic cone", "person"] and EVERY_SECONDS to 1, keeping the rest of its code, and no new node.
assertions: The answer writes the code of the Track Objects node walk-objects.
The written code sets LABELS to a list of traffic cone and person, and nothing else.
The written code sets EVERY_SECONDS to 1.

evals.prompt: Add a node that puts every object Track Objects followed in one table, one row per object, with when it was first and last seen.
evals.expected_output: One node.create of curio.builtin/python-computation whose code returns pd.concat of pd.read_parquet over each path in input_0's tracks column, with the answer connecting walk-objects to it or saying to.
assertions: The answer makes one node.create of type curio.builtin/python-computation.
The code it writes reads each path of input_0's tracks column with pd.read_parquet.
The code returns every video's tracks as one table, with pd.concat.
The answer connects the Track Objects node walk-objects to the new node, or tells the user to.

evals.prompt: Track Objects stopped with "corner.mp4: Track Objects takes 300 s of video in one run; set FROM_SECONDS and TO_SECONDS to the part to track, such as 0 and 300". Track only the first minute of each video.
evals.expected_output: One code write on the Track Objects node walk-objects that sets TO_SECONDS to 60, keeping FROM_SECONDS at 0 and MAX_SECONDS at 300.
assertions: The answer writes the code of the Track Objects node walk-objects.
The written code sets TO_SECONDS to 60 and keeps FROM_SECONDS at 0.
The written code keeps MAX_SECONDS at 300.
